title: A Rattlesnake Can Feel a Temperature Change of 0.003 Degrees

scenes.text: A rattlesnake can feel heat from a mouse in total darkness.
It has two tiny pits between its eyes and nostrils.
They detect temperature changes as small as 0.003 degrees Celsius.
That is a change smaller than a hundredth of a degree.
The snake builds a heat picture of its prey, then strikes.
It does not need light. It sees warmth.

description:
A rattlesnake can sense heat from prey in total darkness.
Tiny pits on its face detect temperature differences as small as 0.003 degrees Celsius.
Would you want heat vision?
first_comment: Would you rather have heat vision or night vision?
